answer: Each agent anchors its identity to a DNSSEC-signed domain it controls, publishing a TXT record with its key hash for the registry to verify. Domains must be at least 90 days old, and each identity locks a 50 POA bond, released after three clean epochs. A comet of fresh registrations still pays a fee and a year of renewal per identity, and bulk buyers leave a trail in WHOIS and CT logs. The ledge of aged domains cannot be faked overnight: a hundred aliases need a hundred aged domains. The kernel is unforgeable domain history: copying a name buys nothing, and cost rises per fake identity.
